questions.q: What does the psalmist call on all the people on earth to do?
questions.a: The psalmist calls on all the earth to sing a new song to Yahweh.

questions.q: What does the psalmist encourage everyone to announce?
questions.a: The psalmist encourages everyone to announce that Yahweh has saved them.

questions.q: Why should everyone tell of Yahweh’s glory and his marvelous things he has done?
questions.a: Everyone should tell of how glorious Yahweh is and all he has done because Yahweh is great, and deserves to be praised and be revered more than all other gods.

questions.q: What contrast does the psalmist draw between the gods of other peoples and Yahweh?
questions.a: The gods of other peoples are only idols, but it is Yahweh who made the heavens.

questions.q: What qualities does the psalmist say Yahweh has?
questions.a: Yahweh is magnificent, majestic, strong, and beautiful.

questions.q: What should everyone do to give to Yahweh the glory he deserves?
questions.a: Everyone should praise Yahweh, bring an offering, and come to his temple.

questions.q: What does the psalmist encourage everyone to say to all people groups?
questions.a: The psalmist encourages everyone to tell all people that Yahweh reigns.

questions.q: How does Yahweh judge the peoples?
Why should the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice?
questions.a: The heavens should be glad and the earth rejoice because Yahweh is coming.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do when he comes?
questions.a: When Yahweh comes, he will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with his faithfulness.

commentary.text: A call to all people to praise God.

Verses 1–9 When Christ finished his work on earth, and was received into his glory in heaven, the church began to sing a new song unto him, and to bless his name. His apostles and evangelists showed forth his salvation among the heathen, his wonders among all people. All the earth is here summoned to worship the Lord. We must worship him in the beauty of holiness, as God in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself. Glorious things are said of him, both as motives to praise and matter of praise.

We are to hope and pray for that time, when Christ shall reign in righteousness over all nations. He shall rule in the hearts of men, by the power of truth, and the Spirit of righteousness. His coming draws nigh; this King, this Judge standeth before the door, but he is not yet come. The Lord will accept the praises of all who seek to promote the kingdom of Christ. The sea can but roar, and how the trees of the wood can show that they rejoice we know not; but He that searches the heart knows what is the mind of the Spirit, and understands the words, the broken language of the weakest. Christ will come to judge the earth, to execute just vengeance on his enemies, and to fulfil his largest promises to his people. What then are we? Would that day be welcome to us? If this be not our case, let us now begin to prepare to meet our God, by seeking the pardon of our sins, and the renewal of our souls to holiness.
